notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.psouffle: The Soufflé program is compiled into a C++ program, which then runs: the time is both, the compilation's added to the run's, though PSouffle's paper times the run alone. PSouffle prints probabilities with eight decimals.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.psouffle: The Soufflé program is compiled into a C++ program, which then runs: the time is both, the compilation's added to the run's, though PSouffle's paper times the run alone. PSouffle prints probabilities with eight decimals.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.psouffle: The Soufflé program is compiled into a C++ program, which then runs: the time is both, the compilation's added to the run's, though PSouffle's paper times the run alone. PSouffle prints probabilities with eight decimals.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

;; scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a hash

;; coins; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from the

;; module's level (`display-pmf`), given the evidence; the program prints
;; `roulette K true P` and `roulette K false P` for the K-th query.

;; run as a query of its own (it runs each expression of the module as one).
(define-syntax-rule (statement e ...) (define-values () (begin e ... (values))))

;; the tuple t of r holds also where x does
(define (add! r t x)
  (hash-set! r t (if (hash-has-key? r t) (|| (hash-ref r t) x) x)))
;; whether the tuple t of r holds
(define (holds r t) (hash-ref r t #f))
;; whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
(define (probe r t) (if (hash-has-key? r t) (list (hash-ref r t)) null))
;; the tuples of r and whether each holds, (tuple . holding) each, by their
;; values at positions ps (from 0)
(define (index r . ps)
  (define ix (make-hash))
  (for ([(t x) (in-hash r)])
    (hash-update! ix (for/list ([p (in-list ps)]) (list-ref t p)) (λ (es) (cons (cons t x) es)) null))
  ix)

(define (holds-any ix k)
  (for/fold ([some #f]) ([e (in-list (hash-ref ix k null))]) (|| some (cdr e))))

;; head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
(define (choose . ps)
  (let loop ([ps ps] [left 1.0] [none #t])
    (if (null? ps)
        null
        (let* ([q (if (> left 0) (min 1.0 (/ (car ps) left)) 1.0)]
               [c (if (>= q 1.0) #t (flip q))])
          (cons (&& none c) (loop (cdr ps) (- left (car ps)) (&& none (! c))))))))

;; the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
;; a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
(define (facts path)
  (define db (make-hash))
  (for ([line (in-lines (open-input-file path))])
    (define f (string-split line "\t" #:trim? #f))
    (define p (string->number (cadr f)))
    (add! (hash-ref! db (car f) make-hash) (map constant (cddr f)) (if (>= p 1) #t (flip p))))

;; at the module's level (`display-pmf`), read back from the table it
;; prints, or from the one value it prints alone.

    (if (and (pair? d) (eq? (car d) 'quote)) (cadr d) d))

               #:when (regexp-match? #rx"[│|]" line))
      (filter (λ (s) (not (string=? s ""))) (map string-trim (regexp-split #rx"[│|]" line)))))

  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs edge)])
    (match-define (cons (list X Y) x1) t2)

  ;; conn(X,Y) :- edge(Y,X).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs edge)])
    (match-define (cons (list Y X) x1) t2)
    (add! conn (list X Y) x1)))

;; reading the stage before, until a stage adds no tuple and the stages number the tuples
(define (stage-path path)

    (match-define (cons (list X Y) x1) t2)

  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs conn)])
    (match-define (cons (list X Z) x1) t2)
    (for ([t4 (in-list (hash-ref path-by-1 (list Z) null))])

  (list next-path))

    (define size (for/sum ([r (in-list rels)]) (hash-count r)))

        (loop (apply stage-path rels) (+ stage 1) size)
        (apply values rels))))

  (list (distribution (holds path (list 'phenotype_mim_104300 'gene_entrezgene_351)))
        (distribution (holds path (list 'phenotype_mim_104300 'gene_entrezgene_323)))
        (distribution (holds path (list 'phenotype_mim_104300 'gene_entrezgene_590)))
        (distribution (holds path (list 'phenotype_mim_104300 'gene_entrezgene_5126)))))
(statement (report dists))

;; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), drawn once; each rule a
;; concat_map over the relations its body joins, a tuple that several instances
;; give holding where one does (`union`). Query cK asks the K-th query, given the
;; evidence.

(define-type weight (Sure) (Chance p))
(define (draw w) (match w Sure => (True) Chance p => (flip p)))
(define (draw_all fs) (map (lambda f -> (Pair (fst f) (draw (snd f)))) fs))
;; rel with the tuple t, holding where v does too
(define (insert eq t v rel)
  (match rel
    Nil => (Cons (Pair t v) (Nil))
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) t) (Cons (Pair t (or (snd e) v)) rest) (Cons e (insert eq t v rest)))))
(define (union eq rel xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => rel
    Cons x rest => (union eq (insert eq (fst x) (snd x) rel) rest)))
;; whether the tuple t of rel holds; whether one of the tuples that p accepts does
(define (holds eq rel t)
  (match rel
    Nil => (False)
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) t) (snd e) (holds eq rest t))))
(define (any_holds p rel)
  (match rel
    Nil => (False)
    Cons e rest => (if (p (fst e)) (or (snd e) (any_holds p rest)) (any_holds p rest))))
(define (concat_map f xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => (Nil)
    Cons x rest => (append (f x) (concat_map f rest))))
(define (between lo hi) (if (> lo hi) (Nil) (Cons lo (between (S lo) hi))))
(define (size_of rels) (fold (lambda acc r -> (+ acc (length r))) 0 rels))
;; the coins of a probabilistic rule in a recursion, kept by instance across the stages: the
;; instances xs, each (Pair KEY (Pair BODY HEADS)), with the coin of each KEY in table (a new
;; one drawn where it has none): (Pair TABLE' the heads, each (Pair TUPLE HOLDING))
(define (coin_of eq k table)
  (match table
    Nil => (Pair (False) (False))
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) k) (Pair (True) (snd e)) (coin_of eq k rest))))
(define (attach eq draw pick table xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => (Pair table (Nil))
    Cons x rest =>
    (let ((found (coin_of eq (fst x) table))
          (c (if (fst found) (snd found) (draw)))
          (table2 (if (fst found) table (Cons (Pair (fst x) c) table)))
          (more (attach eq draw pick table2 rest))
          (body (fst (snd x))))
      (Pair (fst more) (append (mapi (lambda h i -> (Pair h (and body (pick c i)))) (snd (snd x))) (snd more))))))

  (for ([dist (in-list dists)] [k (in-naturals 1)])
    (printf "roulette ~a true ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #t)))
    (printf "roulette ~a false ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #f)))))

(define db (facts (vector-ref (current-command-line-arguments) 0)))
(define edge-facts (hash-ref db "edge/2" (make-hash)))

(define edge edge-facts)

(define conn (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; conn(X,Y) :- edge(X,Y).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs edge)])
    (match-define (cons (list X Y) x1) t2)
    (add! conn (list X Y) x1))
  ;; conn(X,Y) :- edge(Y,X).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs edge)])
    (match-define (cons (list Y X) x1) t2)
    (add! conn (list X Y) x1)))

;; path/2: recursive; the rules applied in stages from no tuple, each
;; reading the stage before, until a stage adds no tuple and the stages number the tuples
(define (stage-path path)
  (define next-path (make-hash))
  (define path-by-1 (index path 0))
  ;; path(X,Y) :- conn(X,Y).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs conn)])
    (match-define (cons (list X Y) x1) t2)
    (add! next-path (list X Y) x1))
  ;; path(X,Y) :- conn(X,Z), path(Z,Y).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs conn)])
    (match-define (cons (list X Z) x1) t2)
    (for ([t4 (in-list (hash-ref path-by-1 (list Z) null))])
      (match-define (cons (list _ Y) x3) t4)
      (add! next-path (list X Y) (&& x1 x3))))
  (list next-path))
(define-values (path)
  (let loop ([rels (list (make-hash))] [stage 0] [before -1])
    (define size (for/sum ([r (in-list rels)]) (hash-count r)))
    (if (or (< stage size) (not (= size before)))
        (loop (apply stage-path rels) (+ stage 1) size)
        (apply values rels))))

(define dists
  (list (distribution (holds path (list 'phenotype_mim_104300 'gene_entrezgene_351)))
        (distribution (holds path (list 'phenotype_mim_104300 'gene_entrezgene_323)))
        (distribution (holds path (list 'phenotype_mim_104300 'gene_entrezgene_590)))
        (distribution (holds path (list 'phenotype_mim_104300 'gene_entrezgene_5126)))))
(statement (report dists))

# Biomine's graph human_3_oct_2018.zip, licensed for academic and non-commercial use, from https://biomine.ijs.si/downloads/. This header was added for this page and is not part of the file the systems read, whose size and SHA-256 the page gives.
# biomine1.pl: a ProbLog program written in SPPL by tddlog's scripts/problog2ppl.py,
# first order as it is written. The facts and the joins of the rules are Python
# constants, computed before the first sample: each rule's matches a list
# comprehension over the relations its body joins, a recursive component's
# tuples a fixpoint of its rules, and the tuples that the queries and the
# evidence read. Then each probabilistic fact and each instance of a
# probabilistic rule samples a coin, and each instance of a tuple that is read
# sets a variable of its own, in a `for` over its component's instances: 1
# where its body holds or an earlier instance of its tuple does, the last of a
# tuple's instances its holding. A cycle of tuples that read each other does so
# in as many stages as it has tuples, each stage reading the one before. The
# queries are the events of queries_(), asked of the model given the evidence:
#
#   sppl_dice.py PROGRAM.sppl
#
# queries
# component 0 bool query0
# component 1 bool query1
# component 2 bool query2
# component 3 bool query3

from functools import reduce
from itertools import accumulate

yes_ = lambda: true_ << {1}
no_ = lambda: true_ << {0}
all_ = lambda es_: reduce(lambda a_, b_: a_ & b_, es_) if es_ else yes_()
fix_ = lambda g_, x_: (lambda y_: x_ if y_ == x_ else fix_(g_, y_))(g_(x_))
dedup_ = lambda xs_: list(dict.fromkeys(xs_))
index_ = lambda ts_: {t_: j_ for j_, t_ in enumerate(ts_)}
by_ = lambda ts_, ps_: reduce(lambda d_, j_: d_.setdefault(tuple(ts_[j_][p_] for p_ in ps_), []).append(j_) or d_,
                              range(len(ts_)), {})
idiv_ = lambda a_, b_: abs(a_) // abs(b_) * (1 if (a_ < 0) == (b_ < 0) else -1)
# the heads of relation q_ that matches ms_ give; a coin's index for each probability below 1
heads_ = lambda q_, ms_: [h_ for m_ in ms_ for r_, h_ in m_[1] if r_ == q_]
coins_of_ = lambda ps_, c0_: [None if p_ >= 1 else c0_ + n_
                              for p_, n_ in zip(ps_, accumulate([0] + [int(x_ < 1) for x_ in ps_]))]
# a relation's instances, each (its tuple's index, its coin and value or None, its refs); their indexes by tuple
facts_ = lambda i_, ts_, cs_: [(i_[t_], None if c_ is None else (c_, 1), []) for t_, c_ in zip(ts_, cs_)]
inst_ = lambda q_, i_, ms_, ks_, c0_: [(i_[h_], None if ks_ is None else (c0_ + ks_[m_[0]], n_ + 1), m_[2])
                                      for m_ in ms_ for n_, (r_, h_) in enumerate(m_[1]) if r_ == q_]
by_tuple_ = lambda es_, n_: (lambda d_: [d_.get((j_,), []) for j_ in range(n_)])(by_(es_, (0,)))
# the tuples (relation, index) that a tuple's instances read; those that tuples us_ read in turn, where ok_
reads_ = lambda u_: ([(r_, k_) for m_ in of_[u_[0]][u_[1]] for r_, k_, _, _ in insts_[u_[0]][m_][2]]
                     if u_[0] in of_ else [])
reach_ = lambda us_, ok_: fix_(lambda s_: s_ | {w_ for u_ in s_ for w_ in reads_(u_) if ok_(w_)}, frozenset(us_))
# a component's steps, each (relation, instance, stage, cycle), over the tuples of its relations c_ that the
# queries and the evidence read: its cycles of tuples (the tuples that reach the same ones), each after the
# cycles it reads (which reach fewer), in as many stages as it has tuples, each stage reading the one before
cycles_ = lambda rs_: sorted(reduce(lambda d_, u_: d_.setdefault(rs_[u_], []).append(u_) or d_, sorted(rs_),
                                    {}).values(), key=lambda us_: (len(rs_[us_[0]]), us_[0]))
steps_ = lambda c_: [(u_[0], m_, s_, g_) for g_, us_ in enumerate(cycles_(
                         {u_: reach_([u_], lambda w_: w_[0] in c_) for u_ in used_ if u_[0] in c_}))
                     for s_ in range(1, len(us_) + 1) for u_ in us_ for m_ in of_[u_[0]][u_[1]]]
# a step's tuple and stage; the step of a tuple's last instance at each stage; a tuple's last stage and its
# cycle; the step before each, where it is an earlier instance of its tuple at its stage
key_ = lambda x_: (x_[0], insts_[x_[0]][x_[1]][0], x_[2])
at_of_ = lambda st_: {key_(x_): k_ for k_, x_ in enumerate(st_)}
ends_ = lambda st_: {key_(x_)[:2]: (x_[2], x_[3]) for x_ in st_}
prev_ = lambda st_: [k_ - 1 if k_ and key_(st_[k_ - 1]) == key_(st_[k_]) else None for k_ in range(len(st_))]
# events: a fact's; a tuple's at stage s_ (None its last, 0 before the first); a step's coin and body, which
# reads the tuples of its own cycle at the stage before; the step's or the one before it
fact_ = lambda c_, v_: (yes_() if v_ else no_()) if c_ is None else coins_[c_] << {v_}
value_ = lambda a_, at_s_, end_, u_, v_, s_: (lambda t_: (no_() if v_ else yes_()) if t_ == 0
                                              else a_[at_s_[u_ + (t_,)]] << {v_})(end_[u_][0] if s_ is None else s_)
coin_ = lambda c_: [] if c_ is None else [coins_[c_[0]] << {c_[1]}]
step_ = lambda st_, end_, k_: (lambda q_, m_, s_, g_: all_(coin_(insts_[q_][m_][1]) + [
    at_[r_](j_, v_, s_ - 1 if w_ and end_[(r_, j_)][1] == g_ else None)
    for r_, j_, v_, w_ in insts_[q_][m_][2]]))(*st_[k_])
ev_ = lambda e_, p_, acc_: e_ if p_ is None else e_ | (acc_(p_) << {1})
holds_ = lambda q_, t_, v_: (lambda j_: (no_() if v_ else yes_()) if j_ is None else at_[q_](j_, v_, None))(
    ix_[q_].get(t_))

# edge/2: 11 facts, each a tuple and its probability
edge_ft = [('gene_entrezgene_323', 'protein_uniprot_q92870'), ('gene_entrezgene_3375', 'gene_entrezgene_5126'),
    ('gene_entrezgene_3375', 'protein_uniprot_p10997'),
    ('gene_entrezgene_351', 'protein_uniprot_p05067'), ('gene_entrezgene_4052', 'gene_entrezgene_590'),
    ('gene_entrezgene_4052', 'protein_uniprot_q14766'),
    ('phenotype_mim_104300', 'protein_uniprot_p05067'),
    ('protein_uniprot_p01137', 'protein_uniprot_p05067'),
    ('protein_uniprot_p01137', 'protein_uniprot_q14766'),
    ('protein_uniprot_p05067', 'protein_uniprot_p10997'),
    ('protein_uniprot_p05067', 'protein_uniprot_q92870')]
edge_fp = [1.0, 0.677, 1.0, 1.0, 0.564, 1.0, 0.65, 0.73432, 0.811945, 0.376, 0.787585]
edge_c0 = 0
edge_cd = [{1: p_, 0: 1 - p_} for p_ in edge_fp if p_ < 1]
edge_fc = coins_of_(edge_fp, edge_c0)

edge_t = edge_ft
edge_i = index_(edge_t)

# rule 1: conn(X,Y) :- edge(X,Y).
rule1_m = [((X, Y), (('conn', (X, Y)),), [('edge', j1, 1, 0)])
    for j1, (X, Y) in enumerate(edge_t)]
# rule 2: conn(X,Y) :- edge(Y,X).
rule2_m = [((X, Y), (('conn', (X, Y)),), [('edge', j1, 1, 0)])
    for j1, (Y, X) in enumerate(edge_t)]
conn_t = dedup_(heads_('conn', rule1_m + rule2_m))
conn_i = index_(conn_t)
conn_inst = inst_('conn', conn_i, rule1_m, None, 0) + inst_('conn', conn_i, rule2_m, None, 0)
conn_of = by_tuple_(conn_inst, len(conn_t))

# path/2: recursive; the tuples that hold in some world, a fixpoint of the rules
# rule 3: path(X,Y) :- conn(X,Y).
rule3_g = lambda path_r: [((X, Y), (('path', (X, Y)),), [('conn', j1, 1, 0)])
    for j1, (X, Y) in enumerate(conn_t)]
# rule 4: path(X,Y) :- conn(X,Z), path(Z,Y).
rule4_g = lambda path_r: (lambda path_rby_1: [((X, Y, Z), (('path', (X, Y)),), [('conn', j1, 1, 0), ('path', j2, 1, 1)])
    for j1, (X, Z) in enumerate(conn_t)
    for j2 in path_rby_1.get((Z,), [])
    for (_, Y) in [path_r[j2]]])(by_(path_r, (0,)))
comp3_t = fix_(lambda ts_: (dedup_(ts_[0] + heads_('path', rule3_g(*ts_) + rule4_g(*ts_))),), ([],))
path_t = comp3_t[0]
rule3_m = rule3_g(*comp3_t)
rule4_m = rule4_g(*comp3_t)
path_i = index_(path_t)
path_inst = inst_('path', path_i, rule3_m, None, 0) + inst_('path', path_i, rule4_m, None, 0)
path_of = by_tuple_(path_inst, len(path_t))

at_ = {
    'edge': lambda j_, v_, s_: fact_(edge_fc[j_], v_),
    'conn': lambda j_, v_, s_: value_(comp2_acc, comp2_at, comp2_end, ('conn', j_), v_, s_),
    'path': lambda j_, v_, s_: value_(comp3_acc, comp3_at, comp3_end, ('path', j_), v_, s_),}
ix_ = {'edge': edge_i, 'conn': conn_i, 'path': path_i}
coin_d_ = edge_cd
insts_ = {'conn': conn_inst, 'path': path_inst}
of_ = {'conn': conn_of, 'path': path_of}
# the tuples the queries and the evidence read, and those their instances read in turn
asked_ = [('path', ('phenotype_mim_104300', 'gene_entrezgene_351')),
    ('path', ('phenotype_mim_104300', 'gene_entrezgene_323')),
    ('path', ('phenotype_mim_104300', 'gene_entrezgene_590')),
    ('path', ('phenotype_mim_104300', 'gene_entrezgene_5126'))]
used_ = reach_([(q_, ix_[q_][t_]) for q_, t_ in asked_ if t_ in ix_.get(q_, {})], lambda w_: True)
comp2_steps = steps_({'conn'})
comp2_at = at_of_(comp2_steps)
comp2_end = ends_(comp2_steps)
comp2_prev = prev_(comp2_steps)
comp2_ev = lambda k_: ev_(step_(comp2_steps, comp2_end, k_), comp2_prev[k_], lambda i_: comp2_acc[i_])
comp3_steps = steps_({'path'})
comp3_at = at_of_(comp3_steps)
comp3_end = ends_(comp3_steps)
comp3_prev = prev_(comp3_steps)
comp3_ev = lambda k_: ev_(step_(comp3_steps, comp3_end, k_), comp3_prev[k_], lambda i_: comp3_acc[i_])
queries_ = lambda: [holds_('path', ('phenotype_mim_104300', 'gene_entrezgene_351'), 1), holds_('path', ('phenotype_mim_104300', 'gene_entrezgene_323'), 1), holds_('path', ('phenotype_mim_104300', 'gene_entrezgene_590'), 1), holds_('path', ('phenotype_mim_104300', 'gene_entrezgene_5126'), 1)]

coins_ = array(len(coin_d_))
comp2_acc = array(len(comp2_steps))
comp3_acc = array(len(comp3_steps))

true_ ~= atomic(loc=1)
for n_ in range(len(coin_d_)):
    coins_[n_] ~= discrete(coin_d_[n_])
# conn/2: an instance holds where its body or an earlier instance of its tuple does
for k_ in range(len(comp2_steps)):
    if comp2_ev(k_):
        comp2_acc[k_] ~= atomic(loc=1)
    else:
        comp2_acc[k_] ~= atomic(loc=0)
# path/2: an instance holds where its body or an earlier instance of its tuple does, a cycle of tuples in as many stages as it has tuples
for k_ in range(len(comp3_steps)):
    if comp3_ev(k_):
        comp3_acc[k_] ~= atomic(loc=1)
    else:
        comp3_acc[k_] ~= atomic(loc=0)

# biomine8.pl: a ProbLog program written in Julia for Alea.jl by tddlog's
# scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a
# dictionary from its tuples to whether each holds, a Dist{Bool} of the coins
# or a Bool; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from
# the facts file FACTS; each rule is a loop over the relations its body
# joins. `model()` is the queries' holdings, given the evidence (`observe`),
# in the form of tddlog's data/alea programs: Alea.jl answers them with `pr`,
# and its tddlog backend writes their circuit for tddlog.
#
#   julia --project=ALEA alea_bench.jl run --file FACTS FACTS_PATH problog.jl
using Alea

const QUERY = :pr
const FACTS = ""   # the facts file (alea_bench.jl --file FACTS PATH)

const Relation = Dict{Tuple,Any}
const NONE = Pair{Tuple,Any}[]

# the tuple t of r holds also where x does
add!(r::Relation, t::Tuple, x) = (r[t] = haskey(r, t) ? r[t] | x : x; nothing)
# whether the tuple t of r holds
holds(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = get(r, t, false)
# whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
probe(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = haskey(r, t) ? (r[t],) : ()
# the tuples of r and whether each holds, by their values at positions ps
function index(r::Relation, ps...)
    ix = Dict{Tuple,Vector{Pair{Tuple,Any}}}()
    for (t, x) in r
        push!(get!(() -> Pair{Tuple,Any}[], ix, map(p -> t[p], ps)), t => x)
    end
    ix
end
# whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
holds_any(ix, k) = reduce(|, (x for (_, x) in get(ix, k, NONE)); init = false)
# the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
# head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
function choose(ps...)
    chosen, none, left = Any[], true, 1.0
    for p in ps
        q = left > 0 ? min(p / left, 1.0) : 1.0
        c = q >= 1.0 ? true : flip(q)
        push!(chosen, none & c)
        none, left = none & !c, left - p
    end
    chosen
end

constant(s) = something(tryparse(Int, s), tryparse(Float64, s), Some(Symbol(s)))
# the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
# a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
function facts(path)
    db = Dict{String,Relation}()
    for line in eachline(path)
        f = split(line, '\t')
        p = parse(Float64, f[2])
        add!(get!(Relation, db, f[1]), Tuple(constant.(f[3:end])), p >= 1 ? true : flip(p))
    end
    db
end

function program(db)
    edge_facts = get(db, "edge/2", Relation())

    edge = edge_facts

    conn = Relation()
    # conn(X,Y) :- edge(X,Y).
    for ((X, Y), x1) in edge
        add!(conn, (X, Y), x1)
    end
    # conn(X,Y) :- edge(Y,X).
    for ((Y, X), x1) in edge
        add!(conn, (X, Y), x1)
    end

    # path/2: recursive; the rules applied in stages from no tuple, each
    # reading the stage before, until a stage adds no tuple and the stages number the tuples
    path = Relation()
    stage, before = 0, -1
    while stage < length(path) || length(path) != before
        before = length(path)
        path_by_1 = index(path, 1)
        next_path = Relation()
        # path(X,Y) :- conn(X,Y).
        for ((X, Y), x1) in conn
            add!(next_path, (X, Y), x1)
        end
        # path(X,Y) :- conn(X,Z), path(Z,Y).
        for ((X, Z), x1) in conn
            for ((_, Y), x2) in get(path_by_1, (Z,), NONE)
                add!(next_path, (X, Y), x1 & x2)
            end
        end
        path = next_path
        stage += 1
    end

    queries = (holds(path, (:phenotype_mim_104300, :gene_entrezgene_351)), holds(path, (:phenotype_mim_104300, :gene_entrezgene_323)), holds(path, (:phenotype_mim_104300, :gene_entrezgene_590)), holds(path, (:phenotype_mim_104300, :gene_entrezgene_5126)))
    evidence = true
    queries, evidence
end

# The queries' holdings, the evidence observed: Alea's `@alea` keeps the
# observation, and the relations are built outside it, as plain Julia.
function model()
    qs, ev = program(facts(FACTS))
    ev === true && return qs
    @alea begin
        observe(ev)
        qs
    end
end

#lang roulette/example/disrupt
;; biomine1.pl: a ProbLog program written for Roulette by tddlog's
;; scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a hash
;; from its tuples (lists of constants) to whether each holds, a Boolean of the
;; coins; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from the
;; facts file named on the command line; each rule is a loop over the
;; relations its body joins. Each query's distribution is Roulette's, at the
;; module's level (`display-pmf`), given the evidence; the program prints
;; `roulette K true P` and `roulette K false P` for the K-th query.

(require racket/port racket/string racket/match)

;; A statement of the program: a definition, which the language does not
;; run as a query of its own (it runs each expression of the module as one).
(define-syntax-rule (statement e ...) (define-values () (begin e ... (values))))

;; the tuple t of r holds also where x does
(define (add! r t x)
  (hash-set! r t (if (hash-has-key? r t) (|| (hash-ref r t) x) x)))
;; whether the tuple t of r holds
(define (holds r t) (hash-ref r t #f))
;; whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
(define (probe r t) (if (hash-has-key? r t) (list (hash-ref r t)) null))
;; the tuples of r and whether each holds, (tuple . holding) each, by their
;; values at positions ps (from 0)
(define (index r . ps)
  (define ix (make-hash))
  (for ([(t x) (in-hash r)])
    (hash-update! ix (for/list ([p (in-list ps)]) (list-ref t p)) (λ (es) (cons (cons t x) es)) null))
  ix)
;; whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
(define (holds-any ix k)
  (for/fold ([some #f]) ([e (in-list (hash-ref ix k null))]) (|| some (cdr e))))
;; the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
;; head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
(define (choose . ps)
  (let loop ([ps ps] [left 1.0] [none #t])
    (if (null? ps)
        null
        (let* ([q (if (> left 0) (min 1.0 (/ (car ps) left)) 1.0)]
               [c (if (>= q 1.0) #t (flip q))])
          (cons (&& none c) (loop (cdr ps) (- left (car ps)) (&& none (! c))))))))

(define (constant s) (or (string->number s) (string->symbol s)))
;; the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
;; a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
(define (facts path)
  (define db (make-hash))
  (for ([line (in-lines (open-input-file path))])
    (define f (string-split line "\t" #:trim? #f))
    (define p (string->number (cadr f)))
    (add! (hash-ref! db (car f) make-hash) (map constant (cddr f)) (if (>= p 1) #t (flip p))))
  db)

;; The distribution of v, a list of (value . probability): Roulette's query
;; at the module's level (`display-pmf`), read back from the table it
;; prints, or from the one value it prints alone.
(define (distribution v)
  (define text (with-output-to-string (λ () (display-pmf v))))
  (define (datum s)
    (define d (read (open-input-string s)))
    (if (and (pair? d) (eq? (car d) 'quote)) (cadr d) d))
  (define rows
    (for/list ([line (in-list (string-split text "\n"))]
               #:when (regexp-match? #rx"[│|]" line))
      (filter (λ (s) (not (string=? s ""))) (map string-trim (regexp-split #rx"[│|]" line)))))
  (if (null? rows)
      (list (cons (datum text) 1))
      (for/list ([r (in-list rows)]
                 #:unless (equal? r '("Value" "Probability")))
        (cons (datum (car r)) (string->number (cadr r))))))
(define (real p) (if (exact? p) (exact->inexact p) p))
(define (probability dist v)
  (define e (assoc v dist))
  (if e (cdr e) 0))
(define (report dists)
  (for ([dist (in-list dists)] [k (in-naturals 1)])
    (printf "roulette ~a true ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #t)))
    (printf "roulette ~a false ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #f)))))

(define db (facts (vector-ref (current-command-line-arguments) 0)))
(define edge-facts (hash-ref db "edge/2" (make-hash)))

(define edge edge-facts)

(define conn (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; conn(X,Y) :- edge(X,Y).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs edge)])
    (match-define (cons (list X Y) x1) t2)
    (add! conn (list X Y) x1))
  ;; conn(X,Y) :- edge(Y,X).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs edge)])
    (match-define (cons (list Y X) x1) t2)
    (add! conn (list X Y) x1)))

;; path/2: recursive; the rules applied in stages from no tuple, each
;; reading the stage before, until a stage adds no tuple and the stages number the tuples
(define (stage-path path)
  (define next-path (make-hash))
  (define path-by-1 (index path 0))
  ;; path(X,Y) :- conn(X,Y).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs conn)])
    (match-define (cons (list X Y) x1) t2)
    (add! next-path (list X Y) x1))
  ;; path(X,Y) :- conn(X,Z), path(Z,Y).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs conn)])
    (match-define (cons (list X Z) x1) t2)
    (for ([t4 (in-list (hash-ref path-by-1 (list Z) null))])
      (match-define (cons (list _ Y) x3) t4)
      (add! next-path (list X Y) (&& x1 x3))))
  (list next-path))
(define-values (path)
  (let loop ([rels (list (make-hash))] [stage 0] [before -1])
    (define size (for/sum ([r (in-list rels)]) (hash-count r)))
    (if (or (< stage size) (not (= size before)))
        (loop (apply stage-path rels) (+ stage 1) size)
        (apply values rels))))

(define dists
  (list (distribution (holds path (list 'phenotype_mim_104300 'gene_entrezgene_351)))
        (distribution (holds path (list 'phenotype_mim_104300 'gene_entrezgene_323)))
        (distribution (holds path (list 'phenotype_mim_104300 'gene_entrezgene_590)))
        (distribution (holds path (list 'phenotype_mim_104300 'gene_entrezgene_5126)))))
(statement (report dists))

# biomine2.pl: a ProbLog program written in SPPL by tddlog's scripts/problog2ppl.py,
# first order as it is written. The facts and the joins of the rules are Python
# constants, computed before the first sample: each rule's matches a list
# comprehension over the relations its body joins, a recursive component's
# tuples a fixpoint of its rules, and the tuples that the queries and the
# evidence read. Then each probabilistic fact and each instance of a
# probabilistic rule samples a coin, and each instance of a tuple that is read
# sets a variable of its own, in a `for` over its component's instances: 1
# where its body holds or an earlier instance of its tuple does, the last of a
# tuple's instances its holding. A cycle of tuples that read each other does so
# in as many stages as it has tuples, each stage reading the one before. The
# queries are the events of queries_(), asked of the model given the evidence:
#
#   sppl_dice.py PROGRAM.sppl
#
# queries
# component 0 bool query0
# component 1 bool query1
# component 2 bool query2
# component 3 bool query3

from functools import reduce
from itertools import accumulate

yes_ = lambda: true_ << {1}
no_ = lambda: true_ << {0}
all_ = lambda es_: reduce(lambda a_, b_: a_ & b_, es_) if es_ else yes_()
fix_ = lambda g_, x_: (lambda y_: x_ if y_ == x_ else fix_(g_, y_))(g_(x_))
dedup_ = lambda xs_: list(dict.fromkeys(xs_))
index_ = lambda ts_: {t_: j_ for j_, t_ in enumerate(ts_)}
by_ = lambda ts_, ps_: reduce(lambda d_, j_: d_.setdefault(tuple(ts_[j_][p_] for p_ in ps_), []).append(j_) or d_,
                              range(len(ts_)), {})
idiv_ = lambda a_, b_: abs(a_) // abs(b_) * (1 if (a_ < 0) == (b_ < 0) else -1)
# the heads of relation q_ that matches ms_ give; a coin's index for each probability below 1
heads_ = lambda q_, ms_: [h_ for m_ in ms_ for r_, h_ in m_[1] if r_ == q_]
coins_of_ = lambda ps_, c0_: [None if p_ >= 1 else c0_ + n_
                              for p_, n_ in zip(ps_, accumulate([0] + [int(x_ < 1) for x_ in ps_]))]
# a relation's instances, each (its tuple's index, its coin and value or None, its refs); their indexes by tuple
facts_ = lambda i_, ts_, cs_: [(i_[t_], None if c_ is None else (c_, 1), []) for t_, c_ in zip(ts_, cs_)]
inst_ = lambda q_, i_, ms_, ks_, c0_: [(i_[h_], None if ks_ is None else (c0_ + ks_[m_[0]], n_ + 1), m_[2])
                                      for m_ in ms_ for n_, (r_, h_) in enumerate(m_[1]) if r_ == q_]
by_tuple_ = lambda es_, n_: (lambda d_: [d_.get((j_,), []) for j_ in range(n_)])(by_(es_, (0,)))
# the tuples (relation, index) that a tuple's instances read; those that tuples us_ read in turn, where ok_
reads_ = lambda u_: ([(r_, k_) for m_ in of_[u_[0]][u_[1]] for r_, k_, _, _ in insts_[u_[0]][m_][2]]
                     if u_[0] in of_ else [])
reach_ = lambda us_, ok_: fix_(lambda s_: s_ | {w_ for u_ in s_ for w_ in reads_(u_) if ok_(w_)}, frozenset(us_))

# queries and the evidence read: its cycles of tuples (the tuples that reach the same ones), each after the
# cycles it reads (which reach fewer), in as many stages as it has tuples, each stage reading the one before
cycles_ = lambda rs_: sorted(reduce(lambda d_, u_: d_.setdefault(rs_[u_], []).append(u_) or d_, sorted(rs_),
                                    {}).values(), key=lambda us_: (len(rs_[us_[0]]), us_[0]))
steps_ = lambda c_: [(u_[0], m_, s_, g_) for g_, us_ in enumerate(cycles_(
                         {u_: reach_([u_], lambda w_: w_[0] in c_) for u_ in used_ if u_[0] in c_}))
                     for s_ in range(1, len(us_) + 1) for u_ in us_ for m_ in of_[u_[0]][u_[1]]]

ends_ = lambda st_: {key_(x_)[:2]: (x_[2], x_[3]) for x_ in st_}

step_ = lambda st_, end_, k_: (lambda q_, m_, s_, g_: all_(coin_(insts_[q_][m_][1]) + [
    at_[r_](j_, v_, s_ - 1 if w_ and end_[(r_, j_)][1] == g_ else None)
    for r_, j_, v_, w_ in insts_[q_][m_][2]]))(*st_[k_])

edge_ft = [('gene_entrezgene_10648', 'gene_entrezgene_590'), ('gene_entrezgene_10648', 'gene_entrezgene_6653'),

    ('gene_entrezgene_323', 'protein_uniprot_q92870'), ('gene_entrezgene_3375', 'gene_entrezgene_5126'),
    ('gene_entrezgene_3375', 'protein_uniprot_p10997'), ('gene_entrezgene_3416', 'gene_entrezgene_351'),
    ('gene_entrezgene_3416', 'protein_uniprot_p14735'),

    ('phenotype_mim_605714', 'protein_uniprot_p05067'),
    ('protein_uniprot_p01137', 'protein_uniprot_p05067'),
    ('protein_uniprot_p01137', 'protein_uniprot_q14766'),

    0.773, 0.73432, 0.811945, 0.376, 0.787585, 0.822962]

    for j1, (X, Y) in enumerate(edge_t)]

    for j1, (Y, X) in enumerate(edge_t)]

rule3_g = lambda path_r: [((X, Y), (('path', (X, Y)),), [('conn', j1, 1, 0)])
    for j1, (X, Y) in enumerate(conn_t)]

    for j1, (X, Z) in enumerate(conn_t)

    for (_, Y) in [path_r[j2]]])(by_(path_r, (0,)))

;; scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a hash
;; from its tuples (lists of constants) to whether each holds, a Boolean of the
;; coins; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from the
;; facts file named on the command line; each rule is a loop over the
;; relations its body joins. Each query's distribution is Roulette's, at the
;; module's level (`display-pmf`), given the evidence; the program prints
;; `roulette K true P` and `roulette K false P` for the K-th query.

;; A statement of the program: a definition, which the language does not
;; run as a query of its own (it runs each expression of the module as one).
(define-syntax-rule (statement e ...) (define-values () (begin e ... (values))))

;; the tuple t of r holds also where x does
(define (add! r t x)
  (hash-set! r t (if (hash-has-key? r t) (|| (hash-ref r t) x) x)))
;; whether the tuple t of r holds
(define (holds r t) (hash-ref r t #f))
;; whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
(define (probe r t) (if (hash-has-key? r t) (list (hash-ref r t)) null))
;; the tuples of r and whether each holds, (tuple . holding) each, by their
;; values at positions ps (from 0)
(define (index r . ps)
  (define ix (make-hash))
  (for ([(t x) (in-hash r)])
    (hash-update! ix (for/list ([p (in-list ps)]) (list-ref t p)) (λ (es) (cons (cons t x) es)) null))

;; whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
(define (holds-any ix k)
  (for/fold ([some #f]) ([e (in-list (hash-ref ix k null))]) (|| some (cdr e))))
;; the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
;; head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
(define (choose . ps)
  (let loop ([ps ps] [left 1.0] [none #t])
    (if (null? ps)
        null
        (let* ([q (if (> left 0) (min 1.0 (/ (car ps) left)) 1.0)]
               [c (if (>= q 1.0) #t (flip q))])
          (cons (&& none c) (loop (cdr ps) (- left (car ps)) (&& none (! c))))))))

;; the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
;; a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one

  (if e (cdr e) 0))

    (match-define (cons (list X Z) x1) t2)

    (define size (for/sum ([r (in-list rels)]) (hash-count r)))

# biomine1.pl: a ProbLog program written in Julia for Alea.jl by tddlog's
# scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a
# dictionary from its tuples to whether each holds, a Dist{Bool} of the coins
# or a Bool; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from
# the facts file FACTS; each rule is a loop over the relations its body
# joins. `model()` is the queries' holdings, given the evidence (`observe`),
# in the form of tddlog's data/alea programs: Alea.jl answers them with `pr`,
# and its tddlog backend writes their circuit for tddlog.
#
#   julia --project=ALEA alea_bench.jl run --file FACTS FACTS_PATH problog.jl
using Alea

const QUERY = :pr
const FACTS = ""   # the facts file (alea_bench.jl --file FACTS PATH)

const Relation = Dict{Tuple,Any}
const NONE = Pair{Tuple,Any}[]

# the tuple t of r holds also where x does
add!(r::Relation, t::Tuple, x) = (r[t] = haskey(r, t) ? r[t] | x : x; nothing)
# whether the tuple t of r holds
holds(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = get(r, t, false)
# whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
probe(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = haskey(r, t) ? (r[t],) : ()
# the tuples of r and whether each holds, by their values at positions ps
function index(r::Relation, ps...)
    ix = Dict{Tuple,Vector{Pair{Tuple,Any}}}()
    for (t, x) in r
        push!(get!(() -> Pair{Tuple,Any}[], ix, map(p -> t[p], ps)), t => x)
    end
    ix
end
# whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
holds_any(ix, k) = reduce(|, (x for (_, x) in get(ix, k, NONE)); init = false)
# the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
# head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
function choose(ps...)
    chosen, none, left = Any[], true, 1.0
    for p in ps
        q = left > 0 ? min(p / left, 1.0) : 1.0
        c = q >= 1.0 ? true : flip(q)
        push!(chosen, none & c)
        none, left = none & !c, left - p
    end
    chosen
end

constant(s) = something(tryparse(Int, s), tryparse(Float64, s), Some(Symbol(s)))
# the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
# a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
function facts(path)
    db = Dict{String,Relation}()
    for line in eachline(path)
        f = split(line, '\t')
        p = parse(Float64, f[2])
        add!(get!(Relation, db, f[1]), Tuple(constant.(f[3:end])), p >= 1 ? true : flip(p))
    end
    db
end

function program(db)
    edge_facts = get(db, "edge/2", Relation())

    edge = edge_facts

    conn = Relation()
    # conn(X,Y) :- edge(X,Y).
    for ((X, Y), x1) in edge
        add!(conn, (X, Y), x1)
    end
    # conn(X,Y) :- edge(Y,X).
    for ((Y, X), x1) in edge
        add!(conn, (X, Y), x1)
    end

    # path/2: recursive; the rules applied in stages from no tuple, each
    # reading the stage before, until a stage adds no tuple and the stages number the tuples
    path = Relation()
    stage, before = 0, -1
    while stage < length(path) || length(path) != before
        before = length(path)
        path_by_1 = index(path, 1)
        next_path = Relation()
        # path(X,Y) :- conn(X,Y).
        for ((X, Y), x1) in conn

# scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a
# dictionary from its tuples to whether each holds, a Dist{Bool} of the coins
# or a Bool; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from
# the facts file FACTS; each rule is a loop over the relations its body
# joins. `model()` is the queries' holdings, given the evidence (`observe`),
# in the form of tddlog's data/alea programs: Alea.jl answers them with `pr`,
# and its tddlog backend writes their circuit for tddlog.
#
#   julia --project=ALEA alea_bench.jl run --file FACTS FACTS_PATH problog.jl
using Alea

const QUERY = :pr
const FACTS = ""   # the facts file (alea_bench.jl --file FACTS PATH)

const Relation = Dict{Tuple,Any}
const NONE = Pair{Tuple,Any}[]

# the tuple t of r holds also where x does
add!(r::Relation, t::Tuple, x) = (r[t] = haskey(r, t) ? r[t] | x : x; nothing)
# whether the tuple t of r holds
holds(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = get(r, t, false)
# whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
probe(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = haskey(r, t) ? (r[t],) : ()
# the tuples of r and whether each holds, by their values at positions ps
function index(r::Relation, ps...)
    ix = Dict{Tuple,Vector{Pair{Tuple,Any}}}()
    for (t, x) in r
        push!(get!(() -> Pair{Tuple,Any}[], ix, map(p -> t[p], ps)), t => x)
    end
    ix
end
# whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
holds_any(ix, k) = reduce(|, (x for (_, x) in get(ix, k, NONE)); init = false)
# the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
# head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
function choose(ps...)
    chosen, none, left = Any[], true, 1.0
    for p in ps
        q = left > 0 ? min(p / left, 1.0) : 1.0
        c = q >= 1.0 ? true : flip(q)
        push!(chosen, none & c)
        none, left = none & !c, left - p
    end
    chosen
end

constant(s) = something(tryparse(Int, s), tryparse(Float64, s), Some(Symbol(s)))
# the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
# a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
function facts(path)
    db = Dict{String,Relation}()
    for line in eachline(path)
        f = split(line, '\t')
        p = parse(Float64, f[2])
        add!(get!(Relation, db, f[1]), Tuple(constant.(f[3:end])), p >= 1 ? true : flip(p))
    end
    db
end

function program(db)
    edge_facts = get(db, "edge/2", Relation())

    edge = edge_facts

    conn = Relation()
    # conn(X,Y) :- edge(X,Y).
    for ((X, Y), x1) in edge
        add!(conn, (X, Y), x1)
    end
    # conn(X,Y) :- edge(Y,X).
    for ((Y, X), x1) in edge
        add!(conn, (X, Y), x1)
    end

    # path/2: recursive; the rules applied in stages from no tuple, each
    # reading the stage before, until a stage adds no tuple and the stages number the tuples
    path = Relation()
    stage, before = 0, -1
    while stage < length(path) || length(path) != before
        before = length(path)
        path_by_1 = index(path, 1)
        next_path = Relation()
        # path(X,Y) :- conn(X,Y).
        for ((X, Y), x1) in conn
            add!(next_path, (X, Y), x1)
        end
        # path(X,Y) :- conn(X,Z), path(Z,Y).
        for ((X, Z), x1) in conn
            for ((_, Y), x2) in get(path_by_1, (Z,), NONE)
                add!(next_path, (X, Y), x1 & x2)
            end
        end
        path = next_path
        stage += 1
    end

    queries = (holds(path, (:phenotype_mim_104300, :gene_entrezgene_351)), holds(path, (:phenotype_mim_104300, :gene_entrezgene_323)), holds(path, (:phenotype_mim_104300, :gene_entrezgene_590)), holds(path, (:phenotype_mim_104300, :gene_entrezgene_5126)))
    evidence = true
    queries, evidence
end

# The queries' holdings, the evidence observed: Alea's `@alea` keeps the
# observation, and the relations are built outside it, as plain Julia.
function model()
    qs, ev = program(facts(FACTS))
    ev === true && return qs
    @alea begin
        observe(ev)
        qs
    end
end
